main.desc: Bomber aircraft of the largest size and load carrying capacity

United Arab Emirates holds its first-ever elections.

Argentina win the FIFA World Cup final, defeating title holders France 4–2 on penalties following a 3–3 draw after extra time.
A series of mass protests began in Belgrade, Serbia, alleging electoral irregularities in the Serbian parliament and Belgrade city assembly elections.
Pope Martin I, having been abducted by Byzantine authorities from Rome for his opposition to Monothelitism, is tried in Constantinople.

Pope Clement III is elected.

Thomas Paine published the first in a series of pamphlets entitled The American Crisis, opening with the line: "These are the times that try men's souls."
Thomas Paine publishes one of a series of pamphlets in The Pennsylvania Journal entitled "The American Crisis".

William Pitt the Younger becomes the youngest Prime Minister of the United Kingdom at 24.

links.t: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

main.desc: 1792–1797 wars between France and European powers

main.t: Vice President of the United States
main.desc: Second-highest constitutional office in the United States

events.text: A Christmas Carol (illustration pictured), a novella by Charles Dickens about the miser Ebenezer Scrooge and his transformation after being visited by ghosts, was published.

French parliament votes amnesty for all involved in scandalous army treason trial known as Dreyfus affair.
Two hundred thirty-nine coal miners die in the Darr Mine Disaster in Jacobs Creek, Pennsylvania.

events.text: King Constantine I is restored as King of the Hellenes after the death of his son Alexander of Greece and a plebiscite.
The last Rolls-Royce Silver Ghost is sold in London, England.
German serial killer Fritz Haarmann is sentenced to death for a series of murders.
Three Indian revolutionaries, Ram Prasad Bismil, Roshan Singh and Ashfaqulla Khan, are executed by the British Raj for participation in the Kakori conspiracy.

BBC World Service begins broadcasting as the BBC Empire Service.

main.desc: International radio division of the BBC

events.text: Risto Ryti, the Prime Minister of Finland,  is elected President of the Republic of Finland in a presidential election, which is exceptionally held by the 1937 electoral college.
World War II: Adolf Hitler appoints himself as head of the Oberkommando des Heeres.
World War II: Limpet mines placed by Italian divers heavily damage HMS Valiant and HMS Queen Elizabeth in Alexandria harbour.

main.desc: Naval mine attached to a target by magnets

events.text: John Amery, British Fascist, is executed at the age of 33 by the British Government for treason.
Start of the First Indochina War.
British physician and suspected serial killer John Bodkin Adams was arrested in connection with the death of Edith Alice Morrell.
Irish-born physician John Bodkin Adams is arrested in connection with the suspicious deaths of more than 160 patients. Eventually he is convicted only of minor charges.
India annexes Daman and Diu, part of Portuguese India.
The ruling junta of South Vietnam, led by Nguyễn Khánh, initiated a coup, dissolving the High National Council, a civilian advisory body.
Harold Holt, the Prime Minister of Australia, is officially presumed dead.

main.desc: Prime Minister of Australia from 1966 to 1967

events.text: Apollo program: The last crewed lunar flight, Apollo 17, carrying Eugene Cernan, Ronald Evans, and Harrison Schmitt, returns to Earth.
Nelson Rockefeller is sworn in as Vice President of the United States under President Gerald Ford under the provisions of the Twenty-fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution.

Twenty-fifth Amendment to the United States Constitution

Sixteen lives are lost when the Penlee lifeboat goes to the aid of the stricken coaster Union Star in heavy seas.
The Jules Rimet Trophy, awarded to the winner of the FIFA World Cup, was stolen from the offices of the Brazilian Football Confederation.

main.desc: Award for victors of the FIFA World Cup

main.desc: 1984 treaty on the transfer of Hong Kong

events.text: Aeroflot Flight 101/435 was hijacked by its co-pilot; it landed in a cow pasture in China, where he was apprehended.
Aeroflot Flight 101/435 is hijacked to China by its first officer.
Mikhail Gorbachev, leader of the Soviet Union, releases Andrei Sakharov and his wife from exile in Gorky.

main.desc: Leader of the Soviet Union from 1985 to 1991

main.desc: Federally-recognized Potawatomi tribe in the United States

events.text: SilkAir Flight 185 crashed into the Musi River in Indonesia, killing 104 people.

SilkAir Flight 185 crashes into the Musi River, near Palembang in Indonesia, killing 104.

main.desc: President of the United States from 1993 to 2001

links.t: Federal impeachment in the United States

events.text: Space Shuttle Discovery is launched on STS-103, the third Hubble Space Telescope servicing mission.
Argentine economic crisis: December riots: Riots erupt in Buenos Aires, Argentina.
Chalk's Ocean Airways Flight 101 crashes into the Government Cut channel immediately after takeoff from Miami Seaplane Base, killing 20.

main.desc: Place in Lesser Poland Voivodeship, Poland

events.text: Park Geun-hye is elected the first female president of South Korea.

main.desc: President of South Korea from 2013 to 2017

main.desc: European organisation dedicated to space exploration

Russian ambassador to Turkey Andrei Karlov is assassinated while at an art exhibition in Ankara. The assassin, Mevlüt Mert Altıntaş, is shot and killed by a Turkish guard.
A vehicular attack in Berlin, Germany, kills 12 and injures 56 people at a Christmas market.
Antonius Primus enters Rome to claim the title of Emperor for Nero's former general Vespasian.
Byzantine Emperor Romanos I Lekapenos is arrested by two of his sons, forced to abdicate and to live as a monk for the rest of his life.
Emperor Henry III convenes the synod of Sutri to mediate between different claimants to the papacy.
Richard I of England is captured and imprisoned by Leopold V of Austria on his way home to England after the Third Crusade.
Attempting to form an alliance with the Mongol Empire, Louis IX of France met with two of their envoys while en route to the Seventh Crusade.
Cardinal Jacques Fournier, a Cistercian monk, is elected Pope Benedict XII.
The Louisiana Purchase is completed at a ceremony in New Orleans.

main.desc: 1803 acquisition of region of Middle America land by the U.S. from France

events.text: Peninsular War: The Siege of Zaragoza begins.
HMS Clio under the command of Captain Onslow arrives at Port Egmont under orders to take possession of the Falkland Islands.

main.desc: Cruizer-class brig-sloop of the Royal Navy

links.t: Reassertion of British sovereignty over the Falkland Islands (1833)

main.desc: First modern presidential election in France

events.text: Led by George Cathcart, British troops defeated Basuto and Taung forces at the Battle of Berea in present-day Lesotho, leading to an offer of peace from King Moshoeshoe I.
South Carolina becomes the first state to attempt to secede from the United States with the South Carolina Declaration of Secession.

Cheka, the first Soviet secret police force, is founded.
Adolf Hitler is released from Landsberg Prison.

Captain America Comics #1, containing the first appearance of the superhero Captain America, is published.

main.desc: Aerial warfare branch of the Imperial Japanese Army from 1912 to 1945

An earthquake in Nankaidō, Japan causes a tsunami which kills at least one thousand people and destroys 36,000 homes.

main.desc: 1945–1949 Indonesian conflict and diplomatic struggle against Dutch rule

The EBR-1 in Arco, Idaho becomes the first nuclear power plant to generate electricity. The electricity powered four light bulbs.
A United States Air Force C-124 crashes and burns in Moses Lake, Washington, killing 87 of the 115 people on board.

main.desc: Air service branch of the U.S. military

main.desc: Capital and largest city of Wales

main.desc: Serial killer in California in the 1960s

links.t: United States Civil Administration of the Ryukyu Islands

links.t: Second round of simplified Chinese characters

events.text: NBC aired the American football match between the New York Jets and the Miami Dolphins without announcers.
Twelve-year-old Jonelle Matthews disappeared from her home in Greeley, Colorado; her body was not discovered until 2019.

main.desc: 1984 railway disaster near Todmorden, West Yorkshire, England

Pope John Paul II announces the creation of World Youth Day.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 1978 to 2005

main.desc: 1989 honor killing of an American teen in St. Louis, Missouri

American Airlines Flight 965, a Boeing 757, crashes into a mountain 50 km north of Cali, Colombia, killing 159 of the 163 people on board.
Portugal transferred the sovereignty over Macau, which it had administered since the mid–16th century, to China.

main.desc: Large bank robbery in Belfast, Northern Ireland

main.desc: Queen of the United Kingdom from 1952 to 2022

Aerosucre Flight 157 crashes during takeoff from Germán Olano Airport in Puerto Carreño, Colombia, killing five people.
The United States Space Force becomes the first new branch of the United States Armed Forces since 1947.

main.desc: Space service branch of the U.S. military

A mass stabbing occurs in a primary school in Zagreb, Croatia, in which a 7-year-old pupil is killed and six more are injured by a knife-wielding 19-year-old male.

Lamberto Scannabecchi was elected pope, taking the name Honorius II.

main.desc: 1140 battle between the Welfs and Hohenstaufens dynasties

main.desc: Military conflict between the Ottoman Empire and the Eyalet of Egypt (1831–33)

main.desc: Highest award in the United States Armed Forces

Challenger expedition: HMS Challenger, commanded by Captain George Nares, sails from Portsmouth, England.

The Chilean Army commits a massacre of at least 2,000 striking saltpeter miners in Iquique, Chile.

main.desc: Land-based arm of the Chilean armed forces

main.desc: 1910 mining accident in Over Hulton, North West England

main.desc: Neo-Gothic Catholic cathedral in Moscow, Russia

American anarchist Emma Goldman is deported to Russia.
Nepal and the United Kingdom signed the first treaty that defined the international status of Nepal as an independent and a sovereign nation.

main.desc: Treaty in which Britain recognized Nepal

Lieutenant Kijé, the first film composition by Sergei Prokofiev (pictured), premiered.
Lieutenant Kijé, one of Sergei Prokofiev's best-known works, premiered.

main.t: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (film)

An 8.1 Mw earthquake and subsequent tsunami in Nankaidō, Japan, kills over 1,300 people and destroys over 38,000 homes.

"Bloody Christmas" begins in Cyprus, ultimately resulting in the displacement of 25,000–30,000 Turkish Cypriots and destruction of more than 100 villages.

The Geneva Conference on the Arab–Israeli conflict opens.
Lancaster House Agreement: An independence agreement for Rhodesia is signed in London by Lord Carrington, Sir Ian Gilmour, Robert Mugabe, Joshua Nkomo, Bishop Abel Muzorewa and S.C. Mundawarara.

main.desc: City in the West Bank, Palestine

Cubana de Aviación Flight 1216 overshoots the runway at La Aurora International Airport, killing 18.

Operatives of the British Special Boat Service boarded the container ship Grande Tema in the Thames Estuary to detain four stowaways who had threatened the crew.

main.desc: Special forces unit of the Royal Navy

Fourteen people are killed and 25 others injured during a mass shooting at Charles University in Prague, Czech Republic.

events.text: Pope Innocent I is elected, the only pope to succeed his father in the office.

main.desc: Head of the Catholic Church from 401 to 417

Mapuches in Chile launch a series of surprise attacks against the Spanish starting the Mapuche uprising of 1766.

Wagner's Siegfried Idyll is first performed.
Disfellowshipped Adventist lay preacher Felix Manalo begins the new religious movement known as the Iglesia ni Cristo with the baptism of its first members.
The Royal Navy armed trawler Night Hawk sank after striking a mine, with the loss of six of her crew.

Admiral Chester W. Nimitz, appointed commander of the U.S. Pacific Fleet on December 17, arrives at Pearl Harbor.

Admiral Émile Muselier seizes the archipelago of Saint Pierre and Miquelon, which become the first part of France to be liberated by the Free French Forces.

Israeli Prime Minister Menachem Begin meets in Egypt with its president Anwar Sadat.

Pan Am Flight 799 crashes during takeoff from Elmendorf Air Force Base, killing three.

events.text: Cold War: The Marshall Plan expires after distributing more than US$13.3 billion in foreign aid to rebuild Western Europe.

main.desc: 1947–1991 geopolitical rivalry between US and USSR

events.text: General Motors becomes the first U.S. corporation to make over US$1 billion in a year.
The Romanian Television network begins its first broadcast in Bucharest.
RTÉ, Ireland's first television network, began broadcasting.
RTÉ, Ireland's state broadcaster, launches its first national television service.
The Central African Federation officially collapses, subsequently becoming Zambia, Malawi and Rhodesia.
Central African military officers led by Jean-Bédel Bokassa began a coup d'état against the government of President David Dacko.

main.desc: Leader of Central Africa from 1966 to 1979

events.text: Jean-Bédel Bokassa, leader of the Central African Republic army, and his military officers begin a coup d'état against the government of President David Dacko.

main.desc: Leader of Central Africa from 1966 to 1979

links.t: List of heads of state of the Central African Republic

events.text: The first flight of the Tupolev Tu-144, the first civilian supersonic transport in the world.
MacRobertson Miller Airlines Flight 1750 crashes near Port Hedland, Western Australia, killing all 26 people on board.
Puerto Rican baseball player Roberto Clemente (pictured) died in a plane crash en route to deliver aid to victims of that year's Nicaragua earthquake.
A coup d'état in Ghana removes President Hilla Limann's PNP government and replaces it with the Provisional National Defence Council led by Flight lieutenant Jerry Rawlings.

links.t: List of heads of state of Ghana

events.text: Two Australian biologists published an article titled "A Synopsis of the Class Reptilia in Australia", initiating the Wells and Wellington affair.

main.desc: 1980s publication of three articles and its aftermath

events.text: The AT&T Bell System is broken up by the United States Government.

links.t: Federal government of the United States

events.text: Benjamin Ward is appointed New York City Police Department's first ever African American police commissioner.
In Nigeria, a coup d'état led by Major General Muhammadu Buhari ends the Second Nigerian Republic.

Three disgruntled employees set fire to the Dupont Plaza Hotel in San Juan, Puerto Rico, killing more than 90 people and injuring 140 others, making it the second-deadliest hotel fire in American history.

main.desc: 1986 fire in San Juan, Puerto Rico

links.t: List of hotel fires in the United States

events.text: All official Soviet Union institutions have ceased operations by this date, five days after the Soviet Union is officially dissolved.
Czechoslovakia is peacefully dissolved in what is dubbed by media as the Velvet Divorce, resulting in the creation of the Czech Republic and the Slovak Republic.
Brandon Teena, an American trans man, was raped and murdered in Humboldt, Nebraska; his death led to increased lobbying for hate crime laws in the United States.

links.t: Hate crime laws in the United States

events.text: This date is skipped altogether in Kiribati as the Phoenix Islands and Line Islands change time zones from UTC−11:00 to UTC+13:00 and UTC−10:00 to UTC+14:00, respectively.

main.desc: Island country in the central Pacific

events.text: The First Chechen War: The Russian Ground Forces begin a New Year's storming of Grozny.

main.desc: 1994–1996 war between Russia and Chechen separatists

events.text: The final comic of Calvin and Hobbes is published.
The European Exchange Rate Mechanism froze the exchange rates of the legacy currencies in the eurozone, establishing the value of the euro.

main.desc: European system to reduce exchange rate variability after the Euro

events.text: The European Exchange Rate Mechanism freezes the values of the legacy currencies in the Eurozone, and establishes the value of the euro currency.

main.desc: European system to reduce exchange rate variability after the Euro

events.text: Russian prime minister Vladimir Putin became acting president upon President Boris Yeltsin's unexpected resignation.
In accordance with the Torrijos–Carter Treaties, Panama assumed full control of the Panama Canal Zone from the United States.

main.desc: 1977 treaties transferring the Panama Canal from the U.S. to Panama after 1999

events.text: The first President of Russia, Boris Yeltsin, resigns from office, leaving Prime Minister Vladimir Putin as the acting President and successor.

The U.S. government hands control of the Panama Canal (as well all the adjacent land to the canal known as the Panama Canal Zone) to Panama. This act complied with the signing of the 1977 Torrijos–Carter Treaties.
Indian Airlines Flight 814 hijacking ends after seven days with the release of 190 survivors at Kandahar Airport, Afghanistan.
Rwanda adopts a new national flag and anthem.
Taipei 101 (pictured) in Taipei, Taiwan, opened to the public as the world's tallest building.
The official opening of Taipei 101, the tallest skyscraper at that time in the world, standing at a height of 509 metres (1,670 ft).

links.t: History of the world's tallest structures

events.text: War in Somalia: Transitional Federal Government forces attacked the last stronghold of the Islamic Courts Union in the town of Jilib.

main.desc: Ethiopian military invasion and occupation in Somalia

events.text: Both a blue moon and a lunar eclipse occur.

Tornadoes touch down in midwestern and southern United States, including Washington County, Arkansas; Greater St. Louis, Sunset Hills, Missouri, Illinois, and Oklahoma, with a few tornadoes in the early hours. A total of 36 tornadoes touched down, resulting in the deaths of nine people and $113 million in damages.

main.desc: 2010 windstorm in the midwestern and southern United States

events.text: NASA succeeds in putting the first of two Gravity Recovery and Interior Laboratory satellites in orbit around the Moon.
A New Year's Eve celebration stampede in Shanghai kills at least 36 people and injures 49 others.

main.desc: Deadly crush of people at a new year celebration

events.text: A fire breaks out at the Downtown Address Hotel in Downtown Dubai, United Arab Emirates, located near the Burj Khalifa, two hours before the fireworks display is due to commence. Sixteen injuries were reported; one had a heart attack, another suffered a major injury, and fourteen others with minor injuries.
Thirty-nine people are killed after a ten-story building collapses in the industrial city of Magnitogorsk, Russia.

main.desc: 2018 apartment building collapse in Magnitogorsk, Chelyabinsk Oblast, Russia

events.text: The World Health Organization is informed of cases of pneumonia with an unknown cause, detected in Wuhan. This later turned out to be COVID-19, the cause of the COVID-19 pandemic.

main.desc: Specialized agency of the United Nations

events.text: The World Health Organization issues its first emergency use validation for a COVID-19 vaccine.
